name: United Republic of Tanzania

areaKm2.note: asOf 2024. Land area 884,000 km2 (AG.LND.TOTL.K2, mid); high is surface area incl. inland water 945,500 km2 (AG.SRF.TOTL.K2).

population.note: asOf 2025 (World Bank SP.POP.TOTL 70,545,865). Low allows for census uncertainty; high adds one year of growth to 2026 (~3.0%/yr).

activePersonnel.note: IISS Military Balance 2025 p.503 as quoted: 27,000 active. CIA Factbook 2025 ~25,000; World Bank 28,000 (2020).

trainedReserves.note: IISS 2025 as quoted: 80,000 reserves, mostly graduates of the JKT national service (6 months military training); readiness uncertain (low).

supportPersonnel.note: Active 27,000 minus infantry P roles (3,000 + 15,000) = 9,000: navy, air force, crews, logistics, staff.

mobilizationRatio.note: Regional analogy: JKT national service gives a trained pool (Uganda war 1978-79 mobilised ~100,000), limited by equipment. Educated judgement.

count.note: Educated guess. Infantry of the tank brigade and mechanised elements. (context page: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tanzania_People's_Defence_Force)

training.note: Rubric 0.5: volunteers, peacekeeping experience (MONUSCO FIB, Mozambique).

count.note: Educated guess. Infantry brigades; ~1,000 in the DRC, ~520 CAR, ~300 Mozambique (CIA Factbook 2025).
Army list: MBT VT-2 5 + Type 59G 15 + T-54 32 = 52 (low); mid adds tracked light tanks Type 62 66 + Type 63/63A 42 = 160; high adds FV101 Scorpion 40. MBT list gives Type 59 30.
Type 07P 12 + BTR-152 55 + Type 55 10 + WZ-551 10 + Casspir 5 = 92 (high adds BRDM-2 10).
BM-21 58 + A-100 12 + Type 54-1 80 + Type 56 75 + Type 59-I 30 + D-30 20 = 275 (towed 85-130 mm and MRLs). Low for serviceability.
Chengdu F-7 B/N/TN 11 (FT-7 2 trainers excluded); low for serviceability.

quality.note: Rubric 0.5: new Airbus utility helicopters, no attack helicopters.

count.note: TPDF article (2014 estimate): 9 fast attack craft + 12 patrol boats = 21 (high); ageing Chinese Shanghai/Huchuan craft, mid assumes ~15 operational.
Battery conversion at ~6 guns per battery (SOURCES.md): ZPU 21 + ZU-23-2 40 + 61-K 37 mm 120 = 181 guns ~30 batteries (high); MANPADS excluded.

commandQuality.note: Rubric 0.5 minus: competent, stable force; last major war 1978-79 (Uganda), FIB success in 2013.

cohesion.note: Rubric 0.5-0.75: politically stable, national (not ethnic) army.

weapons.note: Anchor 8: Chinese/Soviet 1950s-80s artillery and small arms.

logistics.note: Anchor 8: SGR and TAZARA railways, small airlift.

gdpPerCapita.note: asOf 2025. GDP 209,046,739,334 2011 int$ / population 70,545,865 = 2,963. Range +/-10%. Corrected 2026-10-29: values x1.0376 because the rebase factor was an arithmetic error (0.8005); the right factor is 0.8306 (FRED GDPDEF, 2017=100: 2011 91.478 / 2021 110.130). Figures quoted above are before the correction.

gdp.note: asOf 2025. World Bank NY.GDP.MKTP.PP.KD (constant 2021 int$) 261,145,208,412 x 0.8005 = 209,046,739,334 2011 int$. Range +/-10%. Corrected 2026-10-29: values x1.0376 because the rebase factor was an arithmetic error (0.8005); the right factor is 0.8306 (FRED GDPDEF, 2017=100: 2011 91.478 / 2021 110.130). Figures quoted above are before the correction.

milSpendShare.note: SIPRI via World Bank: 1.16% of GDP in 2025.

industrialShare.note: asOf 2025: industry incl. construction (and mining/oil where present) 29.8% of GDP (NV.IND.TOTL.ZS). +/-2 points.

foodSurplus.note: Recomputed 2026-10-29 under the definition: 0.1 -> 0.36. Formula: surplus = 1 - a/s, a = farm population share of consumers (proxy: agricultural employment share, World Bank SL.AGR.EMPL.ZS, ILO modelled, https://api.worldbank.org/v2/country/TZA/indicator/SL.AGR.EMPL.ZS), s = domestic production / consumption (calorie self-sufficiency). a = 64.57% (2025). s from FAOSTAT Food Balance Sheets (https://bulks-faostat.fao.org/production/FoodBalanceSheets_E_All_Data.zip): production / domestic supply summed over all FBS items, each weighted by kcal per tonne (world median of food kcal / food tonnes per item); feed, processing and non-food uses stay in domestic supply. s = 1.01 (mean 2021-2023, range 0.99-1.03). Mid 1 - 0.646/1.01 = 0.36. Low: a x 1.2 (farm households larger than the employed count), s 0.99 = 0.22. High: s 1.03 = 0.37. Net exporter: production is about 101% of domestic calorie supply. Earlier net-trade reading: Educated guess. Self-sufficient in maize and rice in most years; exports to neighbours. Not from FAO balance sheets.

annualCohort.note: asOf 2025. Males reaching military age per year = male population 34,977,375 (SP.POP.TOTL.MA.IN) x share aged 15-19 10.948% / 5 = 765,875. Males only (conscript-pool convention). Range +/-10%.

roadKm.note: Road list (2022): 145,203 km total (high), 11,201 km paved (mid).

railKm.note: asOf 2017: 2,701 route-km (World Bank IS.RRS.TOTL.KM). CIA Factbook 4,097 km (2022) spans the range. Includes TAZARA (Tanzania-Zambia) and the new standard-gauge Dar es Salaam-Dodoma line (2024).

majorPorts.note: CIA Factbook 2024: 8 ports, 1 medium (Dar es Salaam) + 3 small (Tanga, Zanzibar, Chake Chake). Mid adds Tanga.

merchantTonnage.note: Tanzanian-flag fleet 2,758 thousand DWT (1,827 thousand GT), largely Zanzibar open-registry ships not under national control (low).

supplyRangeKm.note: Educated guess. Truck sustainment; 1979 Uganda campaign advanced ~500 km over months.

draftAnimals.note: Educated guess. Donkeys and oxen (not from FAO data).

nuclearWarheads.note: Non-nuclear-weapon state (NPT); not listed by FAS Status of World Nuclear Forces.

homeDefense.note: Rubric 1.2: familiar terrain, population support, national service tradition.

notes: Modern snapshot, asOf 2025 World Bank data, 2026 order of battle. Counts from the Wikipedia Tanzanian Army equipment list (delivery-based) and Tanzania Air Force Command inventory; naval figures are a 2014 estimate (grade C). Population convention: everything inside ne:TZA incl. Zanzibar. Money in 2011 int$ via derived:ppp-rebase-2011. Infantry P-role splits are educated guesses (grade D). armor mid includes tracked light tanks (Type 62/63). Post-election unrest (Oct 2025) not reflected in the force data.
